rated_messages.input_message: Urges can feel like stormy weather. But if you're the sky, you just let that storm come and go on it's own knowing that it won't last forever.

Reduce your stress by using your next break to list four things that have gone well so far today. It might feel like a bit of effort, but doing this will help your mind to refocus, and help you to feel calmer.
A funny thing about people is that we tend to believe what we tell ourselves. So make sure that whatever else happens today, tell yourself "I can, and I will stick to not smoking!"
Instead of smoking, take 10 deep, slow breaths and count them. Pay attention to what your breathing feels like. If you lose count, that's okay, just start over at 1 until you get to 10.

Think about what is really important to you. Maybe it's spending time with family or a friend, exercising, doing something spiritual, or creating something. Whatever it is, take a step in that direction.

Recent research has found that people who use self-talk when they try not to smoke (e.g. telling yourself 'you can do it') are more successful than people who don't. It might seem a bit strange, but talking to yourself like this appears to really help.
Take one deep breath and see what it feels like to be triggered and choose not to smoke.

Think about your hero, or someone you admire. What do you admire about them? Often our heroes are people who struggle and succeed in difficult circumstances. Now's the chance to be your own hero - by not smoking despite the challenges of stress and strong urges!
Notice what it feels like to see other people smoke and choose not to smoke. Notice what thoughts or emotions come up. Allow them to come and go. They will pass and so will this urge.
Stop! Breathe. What is going on around you? Inside you? Allow everything to be just as it is. Breathe again.
